newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says to auction corn to local users Jan 2.
newsitem.headline: Manila says to auction corn to local users Jan 2.

text.p: The state-owned National Food Authority (NFA) of the Philippines said on Friday it was set to auction 252,000 50-kilo bags of corn to local livestock farmers, feed millers and other food firms on January 2.
"We will sell 25,000 bags of white corn and 227,000 bags of yellow corn to interested parties on January 2," an official from the agency said.
The NFA also said some 110,000 tonnes of yellow corn imported by the country from the United States has already arrived.
Two more vessels with a cargo of 27,500 tonnes each are expected to arrive in the country between December 28 and January 11 next year.
The corn was bought by the NFA for local users at an average $161.10 per tonne FOB on October 29. The private sector usually asks the NFA to buy corn for them to get lower prices.
Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero said earlier this month he expected the country's corn imports for 1997 to reach 500,000 tonnes. --Manila newsroom (632) 841-89-36, fax 817-62-67
